Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Class SqlTokenizer

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.SqlTokenizer
public final class SqlTokenizer extends Object
A pure, dependency-free lexical scanner that splits a SQL string into a contiguous list of SqlTokens tagged with a SqlTokenType. It exists so a JavaFX editor can colour SQL offline without pulling in a parser or touching JDBC.

The scanner is best-effort and never throws on malformed input: an unterminated string literal, quoted identifier or block comment simply runs to the end of the input as a token of that type. Every character of the input is covered by exactly one token, so concatenating the tokens' SqlToken.text() in order reproduces the original string verbatim (see tokenize(String)).

Lexical rules mirror SqlScriptSplitter where they overlap:

  • single-quoted string literals '...' with '' escaped quotes;
  • double-quoted and backtick-quoted identifiers ("..." / `...`) with the doubled-delimiter escape ("" / ``);
  • line comments introduced by -- or #, running to end of line;
  • block comments /* ... *&#47;;
  • numeric literals including decimal and scientific notation;
  • bind parameters ?, :name and $1.

    • keywords

      public static Set<String> keywords()
      Returns the case-insensitive keyword set recognised by the tokenizer, as upper-case words. The returned set is unmodifiable.

    • tokenize

      public static List<SqlToken> tokenize(String sql)
      Tokenizes sql into a contiguous list of tokens. A null or empty input yields an empty list. The scan never throws; malformed constructs are emitted best-effort.
